meeting_header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 60 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Opal Head of ML), Sara Nguyen (Opal SRE), Elena Gomez (Opal CTO)
Agenda: Align on POC success criteria, define latency/throughput SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), agree measurement plan and pilot timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — Maya from Redwood, Liam our systems engineer, and on the Opal side?
[00:08] Ravi Patel: Hey, Ravi here. I'm head of ML at Opal. Sara and Elena on as well.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Great. goal today is to scope a POC focused on latency SLOs — specifically TTFT vs TPOT and how we measure p95/p99.
[00:22] Liam O'Connor: Quick context: Redwood typically measures TTFT as time to first token from request accept, and TPOT as steady-state per-token time (tokens per second inverted). there is some naming variance in the field so we'll align on definitions.
[00:35] Sara Nguyen: Before we dive, our constraints — most user-facing workloads are sub-second. current infra: AWS EKS, models hosted in-house via Triton, but we are open to Redwood hosted for the pilot. baseline traffic is about 12 qps peaks, avg 6 qps, with 95th concurrency ~40 when bursts happen. sequences are typically 32-128 tokens.
[00:56] Ravi Patel: success criteria for us: p95 TTFT under 200ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens), p99 under 400ms. TPOT should be ~8-12 ms/token for larger responses.
[01:10] Maya Chen: That's helpful. a couple clarifying q's: are those client-side SLOs end-to-end (including network, client parsing) or backend-only?
[01:18] Elena Gomez: We mean perceived latency — end-to-end from our API gateway to first token to client. but for debugging we want backend-only numbers too.
[01:26] Liam O'Connor: We'll capture both. measurement plan idea: run replay of production traces through Redwood pipeline (hosted and dedicated) and record TTFT p50/p95/p99 and TPOT p50/p95/p99, plus system metrics (GPU util, mem, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate).
[01:45] Sara Nguyen: How do you handle batching and queueing? our worry is that batching for cost efficiency will spike TTFT.
[01:51] Liam O'Connor: Right — tradeoff. Redwood's runtime has continuous batching and latency SLO controls: you can set a max delay threshold and a max batch size; we can tune policies per route. For the pilot we'll test these knobs and show cost vs tail-latency curves.
[02:06] Ravi Patel: Also TTFT vs TPOT naming, we've seen TPOT defined as 'time per token' and also 'throughput per token' in other docs which is confusing. can you confirm units you'll report?
[02:15] Maya Chen: We'll report TPOT as ms/token (lower is better) and throughput as tokens/sec for clarity. deliverable will include both.
[02:22] Elena Gomez: What about cold-starts / KV cache warmup? our prompts often use long context so prefix caching matters.
[02:29] Liam O'Connor: We'll include warm and cold-run variants: (a) empty KV cache, (b) warmed cache using typical prefixes. That will surface TTFT differences on first request vs subsequent streaming tokens.
[02:41] Sara Nguyen: Measurement window? We want stable numbers, not flukes from network jitter.
[02:45] Liam O'Connor: Recommend 72-hour production trace replay + microbenchmarks: 10k synthetic short prompts and 5k long prompts with varying concurrency levels (1, 10, 40). We'll capture percentiles and standard deviation.
[02:59] Ravi Patel: For percentile targets we care most about p95 and p99; p99 is really critical for our SLAs.
[03:05] Maya Chen: Noted. we'll instrument p50/p90/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT plus error rates and tail-degradation signals.
[03:12] Sara Nguyen: On instrumentation, will you provide the raw telemetry? we need logs to ingest into our datadog.
[03:17] Liam O'Connor: Yes — Redwood will provide CSVs and open telemetry traces (or JSON) with timestamps aligned. there may be a small difference in naming from your telemetry but we'll map fields.
[03:27] Elena Gomez: Security question: can we run pilot in our VPC or must we use Redwood hosted?
[03:31] Maya Chen: Options: Redwood hosted (fastest to run), Dedicated reserved capacity (isolated GPU pools in customer VPC via Direct Connect) or Private deployment for on-prem. For this POC we can do hosted then a quick dedicated pilot if you want to validate isolation.
[03:44] Ravi Patel: For compliance we want audit logs and SSO. we'll need SOC2 docs and SAML details.
[03:50] Maya Chen: I'll attach the compliance pack. next step we'll share security/SSO docs and our SOC2 report.
[03:56] Sara Nguyen: Benchmarks — what's the pass/fail criteria for the POC?
[04:00] Liam O'Connor: Suggested pass: for test traffic (mirrored production), p95 TTFT <= 200ms for <=64 token prompts and p99 <= 400ms, TPOT <= 12 ms/token for longer sequences, and system stability (no OOMs, errors <0.1%). We can adjust thresholds with you.
[04:15] Ravi Patel: Cost is also a factor. we'd like Redwood to show cost-per-1M-tokens at the pilot configs.
[04:20] Maya Chen: We'll include cost estimates across batch policies and quantization levels.
[04:25] Elena Gomez: Timeline?
[04:27] Maya Chen: Proposed timeline: you share traces by 2026-03-15; Redwood runs a 2-day hosted baseline (3 runs) and a 2-day dedicated pilot if you opt-in; results review the week of 2026-03-22.
[04:40] Ravi Patel: That works. who owns the traffic replayer script?
[04:43] Liam O'Connor: We'll share a replayer (Python script) and a template for request headers to ensure timestamps preserved. you'll upload traces to the secure bucket we provide.
[04:52] Sara Nguyen: Any special handling for streaming vs non-streaming prompts? some endpoints use streaming only.
[04:57] Liam O'Connor: We'll benchmark both streaming TTFT (time to first token) and streaming throughput (tokens/sec during stream). Non-streaming batch completes are measured by total latency.
[05:07] Maya Chen: A couple of gotchas: network egress can add 20-60ms depending on region; we'll report both edge-to-edge and backend-only numbers. Also model quantization may change TPOT but slightly increase TTFT due to different kernels — we'll quantify that.
[05:25] Ravi Patel: Good. please annotate what parts of the measurement are in our control vs Redwood's.
[05:30] Maya Chen: We'll deliver a measurement plan doc that lists control variables: network path, batch policy, model variant, quantization/checkpoint, KV cache state, request size distribution.
[05:40] Elena Gomez: Are there standard latency SLO dashboards you provide?
[05:43] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console will show per-route p50/p95/p99, per-token cost, batch stats, and trace links. we'll give demo access to a sandbox org.
[05:51] Sara Nguyen: Ok next steps recap?
[05:54] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Maya sends benchmark template, security pack, and replayer instructions by Fri 2026-03-13. 2) Opal uploads 72h traces and traffic profile by Mon 2026-03-15. 3) Redwood runs hosted baseline (2 days) and optionally dedicated pilot (2 days) — results reviewed week of 2026-03-22. 4) Follow-up to discuss cost and contract if pilot meets SLOs.
[06:18] Ravi Patel: Thanks all. excited to see the numbers.
[06:20] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing.
[06:23] (call ends)
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors; speaker labels mostly accurate. Mentioned artifacts: benchmark_template.csv (to be shared), security_pack_redwood.pdf, replayer_script.py (link), demo access to Redwood Console sandbox.
